title: [3.x] Large lag spikes when using ResourceLoader in background thread or load_interactive in foreground thread.
body:
### Tested versions

- Not reproducible in 3.3.x

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot 3.6.2

### Issue description

Years ago I created code to load scenes in a background thread, so they are immediately ready to swap in when the player switches scenes. This was working perfectly. There were zero lag while scenes loaded in the background, and the new scene swapped in instantly.

I just noticed this same code in newer versions of 3.x is now leading to massive foreground lag spikes whenever a scene has loaded in the background thread.

The code looked like this:

```gdscript
func _load_adjacent_rooms():
    var rooms_to_load = [] # Code not relevant, assume it's a list of adjacent rooms we want to load their scenes
    
    var room_load_thread = Thread.new()
    room_load_thread.start(self, "_load_rooms_in_background_thread", rooms_to_load)

func _load_rooms_in_background_thread(rooms_to_load):
    for room_name in rooms_to_load:
        # If the next line is removed, the lag spikes stop.
        var packed_scene = ResourceLoader.load(current_scene_rooms[room_name]["scene_path"], "", true)
        current_scene_rooms[room_name]["packed_scene"] = packed_scene
        current_scene_rooms[room_name]["is_loading_in_thread"] = false
    call_deferred("_resume_room_load")

func _resume_room_load():
    if room_load_thread:
        room_load_thread.wait_to_finish()
        room_load_thread = null
```

I tried converting this code to using load_interactive instead and polling in `_process()`, but I get the exact same lag spike on a single `_process()` frame when each scene is done loading.

I'm not even instancing the scene, just loading it as a packed scene into memory!

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create multiple scenes with enough embedded resources that they can cause a noticeable lag spike in the main thread if loaded synchronously on the main thread. (physics, scripts, sprites)
2. Attempt to load them in background thread, or through polling, without causing lag spikes in the main thread.
